forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: West of England Joint Committee reports exhausted general reserves; budget needs Combined Authority subsidy
news_drafts.lead:
The West of England Joint Committee's general reserves are exhausted, and its budget can be balanced only with a subsidy from the West of England Combined Authority, according to a report to a joint meeting of the two bodies on 23 October 2026.

The statement is in the risk section of the report on the Joint Committee's budget and change requests, item 08 on the agenda. It says the position "links to the ongoing reducing general reserves position, which is now exhausted and requires a subsidy from the Combined Authority to balance".

The report as verified gives no figure for the size of the subsidy or for the reserves at earlier dates. It does not set out in the material seen here when the Joint Committee's reserves ran out.

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 11A - App 1 Draft MCA Capital Strategy 2728
findings.headline: The Combined Authority currently holds no commercial investments.
findings.detail: The paper says holdings in pooled funds, bonds, shares or similar instruments are treated as treasury investments, not commercial investments. It also states service investments are approved through the Non-Treasury Investment Strategy.
findings.matters: Lenders and finance directors watching councils with commercial property or other commercial exposure will want to know where an authority has none.
findings.quote: The Combined Authority currently does not hold any commercial investments.

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 11A - App 1 Draft MCA Capital Strategy 2728
findings.headline: Financing costs are shown at £1.567m in each of the 2028/29 and 2029/30 budgets, against £0 in earlier years, with the proportion of net revenue stream still to be confirmed.
findings.detail: Financing costs cover interest on loans and MRP. The paper shows the proportion of net revenue stream as 0% up to 2027/28 and tbc from 2028/29.
findings.matters: A finance director can compare when a new authority's revenue costs of borrowing begin and how large they are relative to its funding.
findings.figures: Financing costs £0 (2025/26 to 2027/28), £1.567m (2028/29 budget), £1.567m (2029/30 budget); proportion of net revenue stream 0% to 2027/28, tbc thereafter
findings.quote: The net annual charge is known as financing costs; this is compared to the net revenue stream

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 11A - App 1 Draft MCA Capital Strategy 2728
findings.headline: Forecast borrowing of £13.892m at 31.3.2030 is shown against a liability benchmark of £44.420m.
findings.detail: The paper states the MCA expects to remain borrowed within its liability benchmark. It notes that actual external borrowing may stay below the benchmark in the short to medium term because of the internal borrowing first approach.
findings.matters: The gap between forecast borrowing and the benchmark indicates how much future borrowing the MCA's capital plans imply, which lenders can use to gauge future demand.
findings.quote: The table shows that the Mayoral Combined Authority expects to remain borrowed well within its liability benchmark.

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 11A - App 1 Draft MCA Capital Strategy 2728
findings.headline: Treasury investments are forecast to fall from £448.5m at 31.3.26 (actual) to £284.0m at 31.3.29 (budget), with near-term investments falling more than longer-term investments rise.
findings.detail: The table shows near-term investments declining each year while longer-term investments, including pooled funds, move between £47.9m and £68.1m. The paper does not give a 31.3.30 figure, which is shown as tbc.
findings.matters: A falling cash balance reduces the internal borrowing capacity the MCA relies on, which is the reason it gives for the timing of external borrowing.
findings.figures: Total treasury investments £448.5m (31.3.26 actual), £402.0m (31.3.27 forecast), £314.7m (31.3.28 budget), £284.0m (31.3.29 budget); near-term investments £400.6m to £232.0m; longer-term investments £47.9m to £52.0m

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 11A - App 1 Draft MCA Capital Strategy 2728
findings.headline: Capital investments are shown at £217.409m actual for 2025/26 and £293.683m forecast for 2026/27, with 2027/28 onwards still to be confirmed by Committee in January 2027.
findings.detail: The paper's capital expenditure table gives figures for 2025/26 and 2026/27 only. The 2027/28 budget and later years are marked tbc, and the financing table shows debt of £31.347m for 2027/28 as to be confirmed in the budget.
findings.matters: A finance officer tracking a peer's capital programme will see the step up in forecast spending and that the forward figures are not yet set.
findings.figures: Capital investments £217.409m (2025/26 actual), £293.683m (2026/27 forecast); debt financing £31.347m (2027/28 budget, to be confirmed)
findings.quote: *27/28 budgets and onwards to be confirmed by Committee in January 2027

daily_post.headline: The Authority's net cost of services increased by over 45% from the prior year, which the auditor says increased the number of samples needed.
daily_post.lead: A rise in net cost of services of this size is a change in scale that finance directors and lenders will want to see reflected in reserves and budget planning.
